videos.caption: Robot " IRON " Buatan XPENG Ini Begitu Nyata ! Sampai Harus Dibedah Di Atas Panggung Untuk Buktikan Itu Hanyalah Robot Sebuah momen unik terjadi di ajang Xpeng AI Day di Guangzhou, Tiongkok, pada 5 November lalu. Perusahaan mobil listrik asal China, Xpeng Motors, memperkenalkan robot humanoid terbarunya bernama IRON dan gerakannya begitu halus serta realistis, sampai-sampai tim Xpeng harus “membedah” robot itu di atas panggung untuk membuktikan bahwa tidak ada manusia di dalamnya. Untungnya memang tidak ada. IRON benar-benar sebuah mesin canggih dengan tulang punggung fleksibel, sendi yang luwes, dan otot buatan yang membuatnya bisa berjalan dengan gaya layaknya model di catwalk. Kehebatan IRON berasal dari arsitektur kecerdasan buatan (AI) yang dirancang khusus oleh Xpeng. Sistem ini memungkinkan robot memahami dan menanggapi rangsangan visual secara langsung, tanpa perlu menerjemahkan penglihatan ke dalam bahasa terlebih dahulu mirip seperti cara manusia bereaksi terhadap dunia sekitarnya. Menurut pernyataan resmi Xpeng, IRON memiliki 82 derajat kebebasan gerak, termasuk 22 di masing-masing tangan. Artinya, ia bisa membungkuk, memutar, hingga membuat gestur kompleks dengan tingkat kelenturan yang sangat tinggi. Di dalam tubuhnya, IRON dilengkapi tiga chip AI kustom yang menghasilkan total daya komputasi 2.250 triliun operasi per detik (TOPS). Bandingkan saja, prosesor Intel Core Ultra 200V yang digunakan di laptop terbaik saat ini hanya mencapai sekitar 120 TOPS. He Xiaopeng, Chairman dan CEO Xpeng Motors, menjelaskan bahwa desain IRON berangkat dari konsep “born from within” terinspirasi langsung dari struktur tubuh manusia. Robot ini memiliki rangka endoskeleton dan otot bionik yang bisa disesuaikan, mulai dari tubuh ramping hingga berotot. Menariknya lagi, lapisan luarnya menggunakan “kulit sintetis penuh” yang membuatnya terasa hangat dan lebih akrab saat disentuh. Source : Tech , Kompas , 百度 #robot #humanoid #AI #xpeng #china

Hugging Face and its Pollen Robotics subsidiary have opened preorders for Microduck, a $399 desktop-sized robot built for experimenting with “physical AI.”  The 25cm robot contains 15 motors, a camera, a depth sensor, two inertial measurement units, and a “beak” that can grasp small objects.  Its open-source software allows developers to train behaviors through reinforcement learning in a physics simulator before transferring them to the real machine.  Microduck can already walk, crouch, follow a laser, grab objects, and recover from many falls.  More than 10,000 units were preordered in its first five days, roughly $4 million! Initial deliveries are targeted before Christmas of this year in North America, Europe, and the UK. Would you buy one?

Sprout is Fauna Robotics’ small, developer-focused humanoid robot built to work safely around people in real-world spaces like labs, schools, offices, retail, and entertainment venues. It’s designed less like a shrunken factory robot and more like a “human-environment” platform: lightweight, padded/soft on the outside, and engineered to reduce impact risk with compliant control and limited joint torques. What makes Sprout interesting is the “full-stack” approach. Fauna positions it as a ready-to-build-on system where core capabilities—movement, perception, navigation, and social expression—work out of the box, so teams can spend time on applications instead of rebuilding fundamentals.  Sprout also leans into interaction: it can be directed via voice, has expressive features (like articulated eyebrows and LED facial elements), and supports things like whole-body control, grippers for manipulation, and even VR-based teleoperation within a unified hardware-software stack.  Pricing reported at launch is about $50,000, targeting researchers, universities, and builders who want a capable humanoid platform without starting from scratch.#ainews #robotics #Techtok #futuretech

iRobot co-founder Colin Angle, whose company sold over 50 million Roombas, has unveiled his new venture, Familiar Machines & Magic. Its first product is a furry, bear-like quadruped robot with 23 motorized joints, a touch-sensitive coat, cameras, and microphones. The robot communicates through expressive movements rather than speech. A custom onboard AI gives it personality and memory while keeping user data off the cloud. Beyond companionship, it aims to reinforce healthy routines, like limiting screen time. Angle compares its cost to pet ownership, targeting sales next year. Whether it can sustain long-term engagement, where past social robots failed, remains the big question.

I spent days teaching a 3D-printed robot duck to walk. Most of that time, it was falling over. It’s my own build of the Open Duck Mini. The open-source, BDX-inspired biped created by Antoine Pirrone. The whole thing is 3D-printed and runs on hobby-grade servos instead of industrial actuators, which is what makes it buildable on a normal budget and also what makes it so hard to get walking. The hard part wasn’t the printing or the assembly. It was the sim-to-real gap. A gait that walks perfectly in MuJoCo hits real-world joint slop, servo lag, and a center of mass that won’t sit still, and just before you know it, the duck face plants into the floor. It took me 40+ calibration passes before it could take three steps without tipping! What the build came down to: • 3D-printed chassis • Per-joint offset calibration (where most of the pain lived) • Policy training in simulation (MuJoCo / Isaac Lab) • Build guide + docs via Tnkr • A lot of failed walks Real hardware. Real failures. Real progress.

videos.caption: RoboParty built a humanoid robot in 4 months. Now, the full project is open source. Meet ROBOTO ORIGIN, a 1.25 m tall, 34 kg humanoid designed for dynamic movement and reinforcement learning research. Here are the technical details: • 23 degrees of freedom (DoF): Multiple controlled joints coordinate whole-body movement. • 120 Nm peak joint torque: The leg actuators deliver high torque for dynamic motions. • 48 V, 15 Ah battery: Provides onboard electrical power. • Open hardware: Mechanical CAD files, PCB designs and the bill of materials are available. • Control software: The repository includes firmware, motor control and ROS 2 integration. • Robot simulation: URDF and MJCF models support work across simulation environments. • Reinforcement learning: The training stack includes Isaac Lab and RSL-RL, with workflows involving MuJoCo. The robot can walk, run and jump. As someone interested in robotics engineering, I find the combination of mechanical design, low-level control and reinforcement learning worth exploring. Having access to the hardware files and training code gives developers a chance to study the full system, from its physical structure to its learned movements. Reproducing it still requires sourcing components, assembling the robot and tuning the control system. GitHub: https://github.com/Roboparty/roboto_origin Would you build one yourself? #Robotics #HumanoidRobots #OpenSource #PhysicalAI #ReinforcementLearning
